To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the thyroid hormone cascade is a novel component of light adaptation; (ii) thyroid hormone receptor (TR) is a novel nuclear receptor expressed in the retina, and its expression level is regulated by the circadiam clock; (iii) thyroid hormone cascade is an essential component of retinal phototransduction and visual function.
the expression levels of Dio2 and Dio3 are differentially regulated in the retina by the circadian rhythm and by changes in the diurnal ambient lighting.
the thyroid hormone cascade has a novel component in retinal light adaptation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying light adaptation in the mammalian retina.
the role of the thyroid hormone cascade in the retina and its regulation by light.
the identification and functional characterization of novel components in the retinal light adaptation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DIO2 has a role not only during development but also in adult retina and is powerfully regulated by diurnal light and by the circadian system.
DIO2 is a novel component of light adaptation, which may be involved in the circadian regulation of visual function.
the thyroid hormone cascade has a significant role in the retinal adaptation to light.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thyroid hormones, acting as ligand-inducable transcription factors, are involved in light adaptation of the retina.
the thyroid hormone cascade is involved in the regulation of retinal light adaptation.
the thyroid hormone cascade is a component of retinal light adaptation and that this cascade is regulated by the circadien clock.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the circadian clock is a key regulator of the thyroid hormone cascade in the retina.
the thyroid hormone system in the retina is not only important during development but also in the mature retina, as a component of the circadian clock.
the expression of Dio2 is regulated by light and that the thyroid hormone is likely to be a component of retinal light adaptation.
